diagnostic_evidence.quote: for compact sets $K_n, K$ with $K_n\downarrow K$, one has $\capacity(K_n)\downarrow\capacity(K)$

issues.failure_explanation: Sigma_k/Pi_k require the outputs to converge monotonically. (S1) only gives covers containing the spectrum, with Hausdorff error E_n -> 0; the covers are not assumed nested. Hence f(Gamma_n^Sp(A)) need not be monotone. Even when it is, the output tilde Gamma_n - 1/n (accuracy 1/n, shifted by 1/n) need not be monotone. The capacity example invokes right-continuity only for nested K_n decreasing to K, which is not guaranteed. The Lebesgue-measure and capacity examples (Pi_1) and the cc example (Sigma_1) are asserted without any monotonization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the outputs by running minima (or maxima) over m<=n, using that spec is contained in every cover and that the limit is f(Sp). Alternatively, intersect the covers over m<=n. State this in the theorem and examples.
issues.overall_effect: The Pi_1/Sigma_1 (and, under (S2), Pi_2/Sigma_2) claims for Lebesgue measure, capacity and number of components are not established as stated. The Delta_2 and convergence statements are unaffected.
issues.title: Monotone (Sigma_1/Pi_1) classifications claimed although (S1) covers are not nested and the constructed towers are not monotone
issues.why_classification: A short, routine monotonization restores all claimed classifications with no change in method or result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, we can build $\Pi_2^A$ algorithms for the decision problems
A straightforward check shows that this provides a $\Pi_2^A$-tower.

issues.failure_explanation: The only construction given is the min-trick for Xi_Lm^dec, which works because 'measure zero' is a forall-exists statement. For Xi_cc^dec (value 1 iff finitely many components) the statement is exists-forall: exists N with M_n<=N for all n. A min over n of M_n cannot be used, since it would give 1 for infinite-cc spectra. The natural tower, 1 iff max_{n<=n1} M_n<=n2, converges from below to 1 for finite-cc spectra. A Pi_2 tower would need outputs equal to 1 at every level n2 for all finite-cc operators, including those with arbitrarily many components, and eventually 0 for infinite-cc ones. A fixed scale-n2 test cannot do this. So 'similarly' is unsupported and the claimed Pi_2 classification is likely wrong; Sigma_2 (or Pi_2 for the complement problem) is what the argument supports.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat Xi_cc^dec separately: give an explicit Sigma_2 tower (or classify the complementary 'infinitely many components' problem as Pi_2), and correct the corollaries and table entries accordingly. Keep the Pi_2 claims for Xi_Lm^dec and Xi_cap^dec.
issues.overall_effect: The Pi_2 (S1) and Pi_3 (S2) decision-problem entries for Xi_cc^dec, and the corresponding row of the summary table, are unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Decision problem 'finitely many components' is claimed Pi_2 without construction; natural construction is Sigma_2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained reclassification with a new explicit tower for one problem. The recognizably comparable result survives, but table entries and corollaries must change and the matching lower bound must be rechecked.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the capacity of the spectrum is always at least $1$
Each classification has a corresponding lower bound

issues.failure_explanation: The lower-bound proofs use dense families in the limit-periodic class where the quantity is 0 versus positive: periodic potentials (positive measure, dimension 1) and a dense set C (measure 0, dimension 0). The paper itself states that for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators the capacity is always at least 1. So on the class used for the lower bounds Xi_cap is never 0, and Xi_cap^dec is constant (always 0) and trivially computable. The dichotomy used for Lm and dim_H does not exist for capacity or its decision problem. The paper gives no capacity value for the dense sets C and P, so the lower bounds for the capacity rows are unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The other problem functions follow analogously.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the optimality statement to the problems actually treated or analogous (Lm, cc, dimensions), or supply a separate lower-bound argument for capacity (and for the capacity decision problem) on a different operator class. State that Xi_cap^dec is trivial on Omega_DS.
issues.overall_effect: The claims that every table entry, including capacity (Pi_1) and the capacity decision problem (Pi_2), has a matching lower bound on this class are unsupported. The same holds for the Final Remarks claim that all (S1) algorithms are proved optimal.
issues.title: Optimality/lower bounds claimed for all problems including capacity, but capacity is >=1 on the limit-periodic Schrödinger class
issues.why_classification: The defect is a mismatch between claimed scope and proved scope. Fixing it needs either withdrawing the capacity optimality claims or a new contained argument or class. The main lower-bound proofs for Lm and dim_H are unaffected.
